newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end lower in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end lower in slow trade.

text.p: Shanghai's foreign currency B shares ended slightly lower on Thursday in slow trade as foreign investors turned their buying attention to Hong Kong and some capital began flowing into new B shares offerings, brokers said.
The B share index fell 0.518 points or 0.67 percent to 76.448 points on volume of 10.223 million shares worth $4.392 million.
Surges in recent days in China-related stocks listed in Hong Kong had made that market look more attractive than Shanghai, they said.

The Hang Seng Chinese Enterprises Index of H-shares outperformed the blue-chip Hang Seng index, trading up 53.84 points or 4.78 percent to 1,179.12 points in the early afternoon on Thursday on restructuring rumours.
Brokers said the surging H shares sucked a lot of foreign money out of B shares and at least two new B share issues this month had also drawn some capital.
"The B share market is quiet because Hong Kong has surged," said an analyst at a foreign securities firm in Shanghai. "A lot of foreign investors are looking at the H share market."
H shares are shares of Chinese companies listed in the former British colony of Hong Kong, which became a Special Administrative Region of China on July 1.

Sentiment on the B share market was also damaged on Thursday by an editorial in the Financial News which said China's stock markets had been brought under control by natural market forces, rather than heavy-handed government intervention.
"The editorial showed signs that government would like the market to linger in a narrow range rather than fluctuate," one local analyst said.
Of 45 B shares, 38 traded with 16 down, 10 flat and 12 up.
Shanghai Material Trading Co 900927.SS was the biggest loser on one speculative selling shot, tumbling $0.012 or 7.79 percent to $0.142 on volume of 13,000 shares.
Shanghai Dazhong Taxi was the most actively traded on institutional profit-taking, falling $0.028 or 3.14 percent to $0.862 on volume of 804,800 shares.
Shanghai's A share index ended up on institutional support in stocks with heavy index weighting, but trading volume shrank on cautious sentiment due to the Financial News editorial, brokers said.
The index edged up 7.103 points 0.57 percent to 1,252.014 points on volume of 439.1 million shares worth 5.5 billion yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index gained 29.793 points or 0.77 percent to to 3,874.469 points.
Beijing Zhongyan Tango Down Products Co was the most actively traded on speculative buying ahead of the close, surging 0.50 yuan or 10.1 percent to 5.45 yuan on volume of 2.1 million shares.
